module.name: scanner
module.spec: FileScanner follows imports starting from main.drift.xml, parses each .drift.xml as XML, extracts spec elements with their id attribute, processes inner content to extract spec-spec edges (recording each <ref spec="…"> as an Edge with From = the containing spec's module-qualified ID and To = the referenced ID), SHA1-hashes the canonical content (refs stripped, label text preserved), and returns Spec records with module-qualified ID, Hash, Filepath, and LineNumber alongside the discovered spec-spec Edges. See principles.language_agnostic.

FileScanner walks the project directory for text files (see text_file_detection), finds lines matching the D! id=shortcode range-start and D! id=shortcode range-end pattern, pairs them by ID within the same file, SHA1-hashes the lines between range-start and range-end (exclusive of both marker lines) with other marker declarations blanked, and returns Marker records with ID, Hash, Filepath, LineNumber, and EndLineNumber. See principles.language_agnostic.
All hashing uses SHA1 hex-encoded via crypto/sha1 and fmt percent-x formatting. The hash is deterministic across runs for identical content.
Duplicate spec IDs within the same module cause an error with the duplicate ID quoted. See principles.specs_are_truth.
Duplicate marker shortcodes across files cause an error with the duplicate shortcode quoted. See principles.specs_are_truth.
A spec element without an id attribute causes an error. See principles.specs_are_truth.

The scanner scans ALL text files for markers — there is no language allowlist. Any file that is not a recognized binary format (checked by extension blocklist) and does not contain null bytes in its first 8KB (checked by content sampling) is treated as a text file and scanned for the D! marker pattern. This makes drift language-agnostic: any file with a comment line containing D! id=... is a valid marker host, regardless of extension. Binary files (images, archives, executables, etc.) are skipped by extension blocklist first (fast path, avoids reading the file) and by null-byte detection as a fallback (catches unknown binary formats). The .drift/ directory and drift ignore patterns also exclude files from scanning. See principles.language_agnostic for the design commitment.

If spec elements are nested inside a specs wrapper element under main or module, the scanner returns an error explaining that specs must be direct children of the root element, not inside a specs wrapper. See principles.specs_are_truth.

The id attribute in a spec element must not contain a dot. The scanner constructs the fully-qualified spec ID as moduleName + "." + localId. This ensures every qualified spec ID has exactly one dot, separating module from local ID.

Marker shortcodes must match the pattern [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]* (alphanumeric, starting with a letter, no dots or punctuation). This is enforced by the marker regex itself, not post-match validation — lines containing D! id= with an invalid shortcode (e.g. containing a dot) simply do not match and are silently ignored. This avoids false positives on documentation that mentions the marker syntax. Dots are reserved for spec ID qualification, enabling unambiguous disambiguation in CLI commands. See principles.language_agnostic.

Every marker must declare a range-start or range-end suffix as part of the marker line. This is enforced by the marker regex (the suffix is required for a match, not optional) — lines matching D! id=foo without a suffix do not match and are silently ignored. Each range-start with ID X must have a matching range-end with ID X in the same file appearing after the start. Each range-end with ID X must have a matching range-start with ID X in the same file appearing before the end. The scanner reports all unpaired markers at once, not fail-on-first.

Before hashing a marker's range, every line within the range that matches the marker pattern has its D! declaration stripped (from D! to end of line), leaving only the comment prefix. This makes markers invisible to each other's hashes, enabling nested and overlapping ranges without interference.

processSpecContent extracts <ref spec="…"> edges from a spec's innerxml using a strict regex grammar: the spec attribute must use double quotes and appear as the first attribute, in either self-closing form (<ref spec="X" />) or paired form (<ref spec="X">label</ref>). It returns the canonical content (each ref replaced by its label text, or removed entirely for self-closing refs) plus the list of referenced spec IDs in source order. Duplicate (from, to) pairs within the same spec are deduped at the scanner level so validation never sees them. Malformed <ref> tags — those that open with <ref but fail the strict grammar (e.g. <ref sprc="X"> with a typo in the attribute name, or <ref> without a spec attribute) — cause a scan error. Tags with completely different names (e.g. <red spec="X">) are parsed as unknown XML elements and do NOT trigger the malformed-ref check. Refs to nonexistent spec IDs do NOT error here — they surface as TodoBrokenEdge drift items. See glossary.ref for the formal definition of a ref and principles.specs_are_truth.

Overview: ReadSpecContent reads a .drift.xml file and returns the trimmed inner text of the <spec> element whose id attribute matches the local part (post-dot suffix) of a fully-qualified spec ID. Used by drift diff, drift show, drift list --verbose, and writeBaseline to read or seed baseline content snapshots.
Defined terms: specID — fully-qualified spec ID (e.g. "core.validate"); the local part is the substring after the first dot localID — the local part of specID (e.g. "validate")
Requirements: R1. ReadSpecContent(filepath, specID) MUST return an error if specID does not contain a dot. R2. ReadSpecContent MUST parse the file as XML and locate the first <spec> element whose id attribute equals localID. R3. ReadSpecContent MUST return the trimmed inner content of the matched spec element. Trimming removes leading and trailing whitespace. R4. If no matching spec element exists in the file, ReadSpecContent MUST return an error naming the specID and filepath. R5. ReadSpecContent MUST NOT strip <ref> tags from the returned content. Refs are stripped only for canonical hashing (see scanner.spec_discovery); display content preserves them verbatim.
See also: scanner.spec_discovery, build.show_result, pinstore.baselines.

Overview: ReadMarkerContent reads a code file and returns the lines between a marker's range-start and range-end, with nested marker declarations blanked. Used by drift diff, drift show, drift list --verbose, and writeBaseline.
Defined terms: startLine — the line number (1-indexed) immediately after the range-start marker endLine — the line number (1-indexed) of the range-end marker line itself half-open range — [startLine, endLine-1]; excludes both marker lines
Requirements: R1. ReadMarkerContent(filepath, startLine, endLine) MUST return the lines in the half-open range [startLine, endLine-1], 1-indexed. R2. Lines within the range that contain a nested "D! id=" marker declaration MUST have that declaration stripped (from "D!" to end of line) but the remainder of the line preserved. R3. If the range extends past the end of the file, ReadMarkerContent MUST return only the available lines without error. R4. The returned content MUST end with a trailing newline when at least one line is returned; an empty result MUST be the empty string (no trailing newline). R5. ReadMarkerContent MUST NOT strip lines matching the parent range-start or range-end markers — those are excluded by the half-open range definition.
See also: scanner.marker_discovery, scanner.range_markers, scanner.marker_blanking, build.show_result.

ScanResult{Specs, Markers, Edges} is the in-memory shape returned by a scan. The Scanner interface exposes Scan() (returning a ScanResult) and Dir() (returning the project root passed at construction). FileScanner is the production implementation: NewFileScanner(dir) constructs one rooted at dir; Dir() returns the stored directory unchanged. The scanner package is the sole producer of ScanResult values; the orchestrator consumes them and never constructs specs, markers, or edges directly. See scanner.scan_orchestration for the per-scan entry point.

FileScanner.Scan() is the top-level entry point for a single scan. It runs three phases in order, returning the first error encountered: (1) loadDriftIgnore(s.dir) reads drift.ignore (missing file is acceptable and yields an empty matcher); (2) s.scanSpecs() walks imports from main.drift.xml and returns specs and spec-spec edges; (3) s.scanMarkers(ignore) walks the directory tree for text files (subject to drift.ignore and text_file_detection) and returns markers. On success it returns a ScanResult containing all three slices. The drift.ignore patterns affect only marker discovery, never spec discovery — spec files are always reached via the import chain rooted at main.drift.xml. See scanner.spec_discovery, scanner.marker_discovery, scanner.ignore_file.

specFileXML, importElem, and specElem are the encoding/xml decoders for .drift.xml files. specFileXML accepts either a <main> root (the implicit "main" module) or a <module name="X"> root (a named module); the discriminator is the XMLName.Local field. Imports is the list of <import path="…"> children. Specs is the list of <spec> children (parsed via the ,innerxml mode so ref tags are preserved for processSpecContent). Wrapped is a sentinel list that captures <spec> elements wrongly nested under a <specs> wrapper — populating it triggers the specs_wrapper_rejection error. specElem.Attr captures all attributes via ,any,attr so the id attribute is found by name (not by struct tag), letting other attributes be present without breaking the parser. See scanner.spec_discovery, scanner.specs_wrapper_rejection, scanner.spec_id_format.

importLoader follows the import chain starting at main.drift.xml, parsing each file with encoding/xml, accumulating specs and edges, and recursively loading <import path="…"> children. It enforces four invariants per load call: (1) CYCLE DETECTION — a file appearing on the active visitStack (the chain currently being descended) returns an error naming the cycle as "a → b → a"; (2) VISITED-SET DEDUP — a file already fully loaded (but not on the active stack) is silently skipped on re-encounter, so a diamond import graph is harmless; (3) MODULE-NAME UNIQUENESS — two files declaring the same module name attribute return an error naming both files; (4) ROOT ELEMENT — the root XML element MUST be <main> or <module>; anything else is an error. Each load call pushes the absolute path onto visitStack on entry and pops it on exit (defer), so the stack mirrors the recursion depth. Spec and edge accumulation crosses import boundaries: imported specs and edges are appended to the caller's slices. See scanner.spec_discovery, scanner.specs_wrapper_rejection.

parseMarkerFile reads a single text file and returns its markers in two passes. PASS 1 (declaration collection): scan every line in order; respect ignore-span directives (skip lines inside an active span; validate pairing/nesting per scanner.ignore_span); collect each D! id=shortcode range-start|range-end line into a rawMarkerDecl record carrying id, suffix, line (1-indexed), and index (0-indexed). PASS 2 (pairing validation, all-at-once): build starts and ends maps keyed by id; reject duplicate range-start or range-end for the same id; for each id in starts, require a matching entry in ends with end.line > start.line; for each id in ends, require a matching entry in starts. ALL pairing errors for the file are collected and reported in one error (joined by newlines) — the scanner never fails on the first unpaired marker. After validation, hashing happens per scanner.marker_blanking. See scanner.range_markers, scanner.ignore_span, scanner.marker_blanking.

loadDriftIgnore reads drift.ignore at the project root (a missing file yields an empty matcher — no patterns, no error). Each non-empty, non-comment line (lines starting with # are comments) is parsed into an ignorePattern: a trailing slash marks the pattern dirOnly (matches directories only); a slash anywhere else marks hasSlash (matches against the full relative path instead of just the basename). driftIgnore.matches(relPath, isDir) evaluates relPath (slash-normalized) against each pattern in source order and returns true on the first match. Patterns use filepath.Match semantics (.gitignore-style globs). A dirOnly pattern skipped for a non-dir entry; a hasSlash pattern that doesn't match exactly may still match a directory by prefix (relpath startsWith pattern+"/"). Markers under a matched path are skipped entirely; specs are never affected (spec files are reached via the import chain, not the directory walk). See scanner.scan_orchestration, scanner.marker_discovery.

Overview: An ignore-span directive suppresses marker detection for a contiguous span of lines within a single file. This lets documentation about drift markers include example marker syntax (e.g. in code fences, tutorials, or reference docs) without the scanner treating the examples as real markers.
Defined terms: ignore-span directive — a pair of lines matching `D! instruction=ignore-span-start` and `D! instruction=ignore-span-end` that bracket a region in which the markerPattern is not applied
Requirements: R1. The scanner MUST recognize the directives `D! instruction=ignore-span-start` and `D! instruction=ignore-span-end` as a span boundary pair. The directive pattern is `D!\s+instruction=(ignore-span-start|ignore-span-end)`. R2. Lines between an ignore-span-start and its matching ignore-span-end (exclusive of both directive lines) MUST NOT be scanned for markers. Any `D! id=... range-start` or `D! id=... range-end` lines in the span are silently skipped — they do not produce markers and do not count toward the duplicate-marker or unpaired-marker checks. R3. Ignore-spans MUST NOT nest. A second ignore-span-start before the matching ignore-span-end is an error: "ignore-span-start inside an active ignore-span". The scanner reports the line number of the offending directive. R4. An ignore-span-end without a matching ignore-span-start is an error: "ignore-span-end without a matching ignore-span-start". R5. An ignore-span-start without a matching ignore-span-end is an error: "ignore-span-start without a matching ignore-span-end". R6. Ignore-span directives MUST NOT themselves be treated as markers. They are not paired by ID, not hashed, and not linked to specs. R7. Ignore-spans are file-local. A span opened in one file does not affect any other file. The scanner processes each file independently. R8. Ignore-span directives MUST be recognized in any text file that the scanner scans for markers (subject to the same text_file_detection rules). They are NOT recognized in .drift.xml spec files (those are parsed for specs, not markers). R9. The directive pattern and the marker pattern are mutually exclusive: `D!\s+id=` matches markers; `D!\s+instruction=` matches directives. A single line cannot match both.
See also: scanner.marker_discovery, scanner.range_markers, principles.language_agnostic.
